title: LC-MS/MS Untargeted Metabolomics Data Processing
author: Kevin Contrepois
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bf4wjqxe
materials: Metabolite abundances were reported as spectral counts.

steps.title: Analyze data using Progenesis QI
steps.instruction: Independently analyze data from each mode using Progenesis QI software (v2.3) (Nonlinear Dynamics, Durham, NC).

steps.title: Filter metabolic features
steps.instruction: Discard and filter metabolic features based on blank presence, linearity, and sample frequency.

substeps.instruction: Discard features that did not show sufficient linearity upon dilution in QC samples (r < 0.6).
Keep only metabolic features present in >2/3 of the samples.

steps.title: Normalize and impute data
steps.instruction: Perform data normalization and missing value imputation.

substeps.instruction: Apply median normalization to correct for differential starting material quantity.
Impute missing values by drawing from a random distribution of low values in the corresponding sample.

steps.title: Merge data and identify metabolites
steps.instruction: Merge data from each mode and formally identify metabolites.

substeps.instruction: Match fragmentation spectra and retention time to analytical-grade standards when possible.
Match experimental MS/MS to fragmentation spectra in publicly available databases.

steps.title: Perform peak annotation
steps.instruction: Annotate peaks using an in-house library and public databases via the R package ‘MetID’ (v0.2.0).

substeps.instruction: Match experimental m/z, retention time, and MS/MS spectra to an in-house library of analytical-grade standards.
Identify remaining peaks by matching experimental m/z and fragmentation spectra to public databases (HMDB, MoNA, and MassBank) using MetID.
Match Progenesis QI metabolic feature tables to fragmentation spectra using a window of ±15 ppm for m/z and ±30 s (HILIC) or ±20 s (RPLC) for retention time.
Use all matched MS/MS spectra if multiple spectra match a single metabolic feature.
Search MS1 and MS2 pairs against public databases and calculate a similarity score using the forward dot–product algorithm.
Report metabolites with a similarity score above 0.4.
Manually investigate spectra from metabolites of interest to confirm identification.
